newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOOTBALL-INJURY, UEFA HIT FERENCVAROS CHALLENGE TO NEWCASTLE.
newsitem.headline: FOOTBALL-INJURY, UEFA HIT FERENCVAROS CHALLENGE TO NEWCASTLE.

text.p: Hungarian Champions Ferencvaros face an injury crisis and the threat of a UEFA ban ahead of Tuesday night's UEFA Cup second round first leg match against English league leaders Newcastle United.

Hungarian international goalkeeper Attila Hajdu is ruled out along with fellow internationals Zoltan Jagodics amd Tibor Simon. The two defenders would have been given the job of man marking Newcastle's multi-million-pound striking pairing of Alan Shearer and Les Ferdinand.
With four other players are also on the injury list Ferencvaros coach Zoltan Varga is putting on a brave face.
"Of course it is a blow to have seven players out for such a big game," Varga told Reuters. "But I am sure the lads who will come in will do a good job."

Varga's injury clouds lifted slightly on Saturday when 20-year-old midfielder Krisztian Lisztes, the bright young hope of Hungarian football, returned to action in the 1-0 win over Vasas afer three months out with an ankle injury.
"Krisztian is very important to us, he is a genuine talent," said Varga.

However it is not only injury problems that are causing Ferencvaros concern. The club were fined 100,000 Swiss francs ($80,000) by UEFA earlier this month after their crowd trouble during a home tie with Olympiakos of Greece in September.
UEFA have warned the club, which has a history of crowd violence, that any repetition will see them thrown out of European competition.
The club last week appealed to its fans to behave and has promised to tighten security at the ground for Tuesday's match.

Ferencvaros, who found themselves in the UEFA Cup after being knocked out of the preliminary roynd of the Champions' League by IFK Gothenburg, are currently lying second in the Hungarian League and have been given a new lease of life since the appointment of Varga a month ago.

Varga was a star of the famous Ferencvaros side of the mid-sixties but defected to West Germany in 1968. After a career taking in Borussia Dortmund, Ajax and Aberdeen he returned to Hungary only in September after 28 years.

Since Varga took over from previous coach Dezso Novak, "Fradi", as the team is known locally, have won five league games in a row, conceding just one goal, and in the last round of the UEFA Cup won at home and drew away to Olympiakos to earn a lucrative tie against the current English Premiership leaders.
"It will be a very difficult game," said Varga. "Newcastle have a side packed with stars, we have to take away their strength in midfield amd stretch them across the park."
"But we will be prepared. I am an optimist and I believe in my team," he said.
Although he acknowledged the threat that Newcastle's strikers pose to his side, Varga singled out Keith Gillespie as the danger man.
"He is the one who gives Ferdinand and Shearer the ammunition, we need to take him out," he said.
